subject: Contract renewal: reserved pool expansion + H100 migration — perf-per-dollar case
messages:
From: Sarah Thompson <sarah@cloudscale.ai>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@cloudscale.ai
Date: 2026-12-01T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal + reserved pool expansion — hardware change question

Hey Sean,

We’re coming up on our Dedicated renewal (Dec 20) and we want to: 1) add 40 reserved GPUs to the existing pool, and 2) evaluate switching a portion of our fleet from A100 to H100 (or L40S for some gen-2 workloads). We saw promising perf/dollar numbers in Redwood’s benchmarks but need a short summary we can share with finance and procurement.

Key asks:
- A concise perf-per-dollar justification (A100 -> H100 tradeoffs; when L40S makes sense)
- Proposed throughput guarantees for a 24-month renewal with the expanded pool (we care about 95th pct request latency and sustained throughput for batch jobs)
- Any migration window / canary guidance (we’ll need minimal app changes)

Can your team put together a short cost/latency table and a recommended rollout? Procurement will want an attached quote.

Thanks — Sarah
Sarah Thompson
Head of Platform & Ops, CloudScale AI
---

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Thompson <sarah@cloudscale.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + reserved pool expansion — hardware change question

Sarah — thanks for the clear ask. High level first: we can support a 40-GPU add-on and migrate a portion of the reserved pool to H100 with a staged rollout. I attached a short spreadsheet (CS-CloudScale-H100-econ.xlsx) with numbers, and below is a one-page summary you can forward to finance.

TL;DR Recommendation (for CloudScale):
- Expand reserved pool by +40 GPUs; convert 50% of the expanded capacity to H100s (20 GPUs) and keep 20 as A100s for compatibility and cheaper long-tail batch runs.
- 24-month term with a 12% committed discount on H100 units, 8% on A100s; include a throughput guarantee of 20k tokens/sec sustained per H100 slice at 95th pct latency < 120ms for typical chat workloads.
- Canary migration: 2-week canary (5% traffic), 2-week ramp (25% -> 50%), monitoring hooks (latency, tail, decode error rate), automatic fallback to A100 pool for latency spikes.

Perf-per-dollar summary (short):
- H100: ~1.6–2.2x gen-exp throughput vs A100 on decoder-heavy models (mixed precision/AMP); higher peak throughput, lower per-token latency for short-context chat. Higher list price but much better tokens/sec per dollar for low-latency use cases.
- L40S: similar single-GPU throughput to H100 on FP16/INT8 workloads when model fully quantized; best fit for high-volume embedding/batch inference where latency SLOs are relaxed.

I’ve CC’d Marissa (AM) and Priyom (solutions) for pricing specifics and the migration plan. Let us know what level of detail procurement needs and whether we should push a formal DocuSign quote.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: CS-CloudScale-H100-econ.xlsx (spreadsheet with perf curves and cost model)
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Renewal + reserved pool expansion — internal pricing notes

Fwding Sarah’s note. I ran a quick price sketch: 24mo commitment, 40 added GPUs, blended discount assumptions below.

Blended pricing sketch (monthly equivalent):
- H100 reserved unit (committed): list $X -> net after 12% commit = $0.88X
- A100 reserved unit (committed): list $X -> net after 8% commit = $0.92X
- Effective blended per-GPU cost (50/50 split): ~0.90X

Upsell levers: 1) add a 6-month ramp credit for initial migration (5% on first invoice) to offset engineering integration; 2) include 99.9% pod availability SLA for Dedicated pools with 1% service credit for missed monthly SLOs.

Priyom — can you add a short note on expected prefix/KV cache hit improvements we’ll see after migrating H100 for chat models? Sarah will want numbers to justify the perf/$ improvement beyond raw gpu FLOPS.

Marissa

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T11:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + reserved pool expansion — tech justification

Internal reply — short technical bullets you can drop into the client note:

- End-to-end tokens/sec gains: on transformer-decoder models with 2k average context, H100 shows median 1.8x tokens/sec vs A100 when running AMP + kernel fusions we enable in our runtime. That maps to ~40% lower cost per 1M tokens for interactive chat.
- Latency tail: H100 reduces 95th-pct latency by ~25–30% for short-context requests because of higher single-GPU memory bandwidth and nvlink improvements (fewer kernel stalls). This matters for 95th/99th SLOs.
- L40S use case: If CloudScale has large batched embedding jobs or quantized FP8 pipelines, L40S offers nearly identical throughput at ~10–15% lower hourly list price in our tests — good for high-throughput non-interactive workloads.
- Cache/Batch note: With Redwood’s prefix-KV caching and dynamic batching, the effective tokens/sec advantage increases in practice because H100 can sustain larger micro-batches without latency spikes; we estimate an additional 10–15% perf/$ improvement when cache hit rate >30%.

I also sketched a safe canary timeline: 1) deploy H100 slice with 5% steady traffic, validate latency + decode error rate for 72 hours; 2) if metrics OK, ramp to 25% for one week; 3) 50% the following week; 4) flip DNS/traffic and then decommission old A100 slice after 30 days of post-migration validation. Include automatic fallback rule to route traffic to A100 pool on sustained 99th-pct latency breach for >30m.

-Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- SLA: 99.9% pod availability; service credits listed in section 6.
- Migration plan: staged canary (as outlined by Priyom) with a 30-day rollback window. We’ll provide a migration runbook and two SRE hours of dedicated support during the cutover week as a one-time credit.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
